title: Vajont — the dam did not fail
style: documentary photograph, northern Italian Alps, overcast limestone light, grey and slate, fine grain, no text, no watermark, no people
negative: no modern tourists, no signage, no cartoon, no illustration

lines.vo: The dam at Vajont did not fail.
lines.title: IT HELD
lines.image: the Vajont dam standing today in its gorge, seen from below, with the bare grey scar of the 1963 slide on the mountainside behind it, overcast light, no people

lines.vo: The dam was a wall of concrete two hundred and sixty-two metres high.
The river below it ran down to the town of Longarone.
lines.image: the town of Longarone in the Piave valley seen from the slope above, the valley floor flat and built on, mountains either side

lines.vo: But the mountainside above the reservoir was already creeping.
caption: Monte Toc
was MOVING.

lines.vo: Inside it a slab of rock rested on a weak bed of clay.
caption: A slip plane,
inside the mountain.

lines.vo: Water from the reservoir soaked into that clay until the bed let go.
On the ninth of October the slab slid into the lake in forty-five seconds.
Two hundred and seventy million cubic metres of rock took the reservoir's place.
caption: The rock went in.
The water came OUT.

lines.vo: The lake had nowhere to go but over the crest of the dam.
caption: Over
the top.

lines.vo: Minutes later it reached the town of Longarone, and two thousand people died.
The dam is still standing, and they built the wrong thing correctly.
lines.title: STILL THERE
lines.image: the crest and downstream face of the Vajont dam intact, the reservoir behind it filled with rock instead of water
